inconsistencies: #35713 (in-tree test runner and assertion framework) and #35139 (new thread-safe ASSERT macros) both introduce replacement assertion macros for Boost.Test; they must not land independently. Review #35713 first to decide the direction, then rebase or drop #35139. #36843 (adding util/check.h includes across tests) touches the same assertion surface.
Chain: #35911 is explicitly based on #36087 (AssertUnreachable); review #36087 first, #35911 second.
#36794, #36831 and #36852 are three instalments of the same test-isolation effort tracked in #36692; same band, and reviewing one establishes the pattern for the other two.

#36730, #36729 and #36846 all fix the same class of bug (code assuming a socket read returns a whole message), all reproduced via the forced-chunking patch in #36724. Review #36730 first: it is in the shared framework transport and affects every p2p functional test; the other two are single-test fixes.
#32554 supersedes #32457, which proposed swapping the binary fixture for another static mainnet block; #32457 should be closed if #32554 is accepted.
Stated prerequisites that fix review order: #36786 depends on #36765; #36808 is based on #36807 and #36844; #35442 depends on #35433; #36781 is based on #36743; #35911 is based on #36087.

#35774 (macOS arm64), #36147 (BSD VMs), #36082 (Guix builds) and #33145 (silent merge check) all add new recurring CI jobs. They compete for the same CI budget and should be weighed together; #35774 has the clearest evidence of a regression that reached master (#35771).
#36437 is a prerequisite for the follow-up orphanage hole fixes in #36506, so it should not sit behind unrelated coverage work.
result.notes: Only two PRs are placed at P1: the category's own ordering puts trustworthy CI signal first, and those are the two whose absence demonstrably costs signal across the whole project (workflow-wide spurious failures; a harness that found a live relay bug). The benchmark PRs (#32554, #35827, #34360) were aligned at P3 so that none of them outranks coverage or flake work. Linter/include/style PRs are clustered at the bottom of P4; they are in-scope for this category but are judged on their own terms as hygiene with no effect on test signal.
